objective: Reduce per-observation launch and memory-copy overhead with a fused FP32 Triton optimizer while preserving the v2 mathematical experiment. No covariance, optimizer change, new loss scale or privileged information.
hypothesis: V2 single-candidate replay needs roughly1.5s Adam and2.1s tangent for65536observations of a5377parameter MLP. A candidate-owned fused kernel holding state over16observations should avoid many tiny forward/backward/update/copy launches. This bottleneck attribution is a hypothesis until measured end-to-end.
reference: cleanrl/plasticity/predictive_transport_stream_v2.py after same-state validity-mask parity fix; jobs5807contracts38passed,5808stationary/5809stress refined224grids completed.
algorithm: Exactly the five v2 arms adam/predictive/tangent/implicit/robust and their moment masses, beta2=.999,eps1e-8, current noisy labels only. FP32 current/previous weights and moments, no Jacobian-ratio gate. Robust retains its different pseudo-Huber objective. No beta/lr or method changes for v3.

execution.kernel: One CTA per candidate, analytical three-layer forward/output-Jacobian and optimizer in one Triton kernel. Process16observations per captured launch where supported. Candidate-owned stream counters prevent shared-index write/read races. Preserve historical nonfinite flags across inner-loop steps.
execution.precision: CUDA FP32, TF32 disabled. Rounded/libdevice operations and FP contraction disabled initially. No CPU/eager/FP64 learning fallback; eager CUDA v2 is audit-only.
execution.autocull: None on full65536sample diagnostic streams; no retries or short training runs.

selection.criterion: Same duration-weighted fullstream clean validation and exclusive global test barrier as v2; independentselection allarms; nofinitecandidatefiltering, no test-basedrescue. Same retained paireddatahashes.
selection.comparison: Compare v2/v3 selected risk and coordinates as well as K=1 fullstream event timing. Different reduction orders need not be bitidentical, but substantial error/selection changes need explanation; no faster wrong solver credited.

verification: Independent v2 CUDA FP32 eager math (itself checked against FP64 autograd/denseimplicit solve), same-state validity-mask equality before exclusions, original rtol3e-3 atol3e-5. Compare fused16stepblocks to sequentialsteps, exact fused CUDAgraph replay, complete state rollback, candidate-owned indices, transientNaNisolation and old/newweightlifetimes.
performance: Full224candidate update/report walltime separately from selected K=1 CUDAevent fullstream replay excluding construction/capture/validation/test/checkpoint IO. Do not compare different grids as if equalwork. Include forward/Jacobian counts and runtime source/data fingerprints.

occupancy_experiment.reason: Initial fused runs5812/5813 preserve all selected coordinates and sustained risk within5.3e-6, but improve K1 latency only for Adam/tangent while slowing the other arms. Test kernel occupancy rather than assume launch fusion is sufficient.
occupancy_experiment.controls: Every combination of five arms, K1 or K224, and warps4/8/16. Same stationary seed1 complete65536stream, originalv2 validation-selected K1 tuple or full224grid. No new learning-hyperparameter selection. Capture parity required for each execution configuration.
occupancy_experiment.measurements: CUDAevent complete-stream replay time, registers/thread, spill count, shared memory, endpoint validation vector as a fidelity check. No held-out test scoring. Keep all rejected execution configurations visible.
occupancy_experiment.retention: Choose execution settings from measured latency/aggregate throughput subject to fidelity, not test accuracy. A retained source change gets its own version and full paired-stream confirmation.

limits: Execution optimization, not a novel optimizer. Same existingseed/task adaptation, no PPO orglobaloptimalityclaim. Fused precision may cause minortrajectorydifferences. Largecandidategrid throughput and K1 latency are different metrics.
